note: Four defects in the last programme were found only in production deployment acceptance, after a full deployment had already been stood up. Every cheaper job missed them for one reason: those jobs run under the development autoloader, with development dependencies present, in a writable tree. This lane builds the artifact the way a release builds it — the archived source, `composer install --no-dev --classmap-authoritative`, a read-only tree with a writable storage volume, and the real console binary — and runs each of those four defects as a regression case inside it. A case declared here and not executed by tools/deployed-artifact-lane.sh fails the lane, because a drill leg that never ran inside the image is itself one of the four defects.

environment.console: bin/kumwe, executed from inside the artifact
environment.database: none: the lane runs before one is stood up, and no defect it reproduces needs one. The drills that need a database stay in deployment acceptance.

cases.title: The artifact refuses a write to its own tree and keeps one writable volume
cases.why: Every other case in this lane is only meaningful if the tree really is read-only. This one proves the precondition rather than assuming it: the tree carries no write bit, storage stays writable the way a deployment mounts it, and the released selection carries the drill directory and not the test suite.

cases.title: Package admission costs the bytes that arrive, not the ceiling per entry
cases.why: The zip reader asked for the maximum entry size plus one on every entry, so three files weighing a few kilobytes cost 192 MiB against a 256 MiB image limit and deployment acceptance failed identically on all three engines. The unit suite pins the cost, but it pins it under a development memory limit; this case pins it under the image's.

cases.title: The production classmap resolves the application, and the drill loader resolves the drills
cases.why: The image installs with --no-dev and an authoritative classmap, so nothing under the test namespace is loadable there. A drill that gained a collaborator without gaining a require line died with class-not-found after the deployment was already up, and every cheaper job passed because they all run under the development autoloader.

cases.title: The real console binary loads its whole boot path inside the artifact
cases.reproduces: the missing production autoloader path, at the binary rather than at a class
cases.why: bin/kumwe reaches further into the tree than anything else: bootstrap, the composition root, the typed configuration and every service the requested command touches, all resolved by an authoritative classmap. This lane is database-free on purpose, because it has to fail before a deployment is stood up and none of the four defects needs a database, so the case asserts what that can honestly prove: the binary executes its boot path, and if it stops it stops on the infrastructure it was pointed at rather than on something it could not load.

cases.title: Every declared drill leg loads and runs inside the artifact
cases.reproduces: a drill leg that had never executed inside the deployed image
cases.why: A leg can be declared, wired into a workflow and still never execute where it matters. This case executes each declared drill entry point inside the artifact and resolves the whole test-namespace class graph each one reaches, so a harness cannot acquire a collaborator without acquiring a way to fail here first.

cases.title: A rotation never strands an envelope, and a stranded one fails loudly
cases.why: A site-wide rotation moved every stored envelope onto a key whose material existed only inside one process, and nothing noticed because a stranded envelope hashes exactly like a readable one. This case proves the ring opens what the previous key sealed, proves the stranded envelope is byte-identical to the readable one so a digest could never have caught it, proves the missing key is a named refusal rather than a corrupt-ciphertext error, and proves the rotation reverses through the same supported operation.
